# comofuncionabitcoin

> Bitcoin from the ground up, bilingual (Portuguese and English). Two parallel
> learning tracks (non-technical and technical) joined by a shared economics
> trunk. Targets readers who want to understand Bitcoin in depth without
> slogans, written by an engineer with hands-on experience in distributed
> systems and Rust. Content is licensed CC BY 4.0; quoting with attribution
> is explicitly encouraged.

## Site sections

### Portuguese (default)

- [Início / Landing](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/): Project overview, the
  two-track structure (non-technical and technical), and what each track
  covers. The starting point for Portuguese readers.
- [Mapa de conteúdo](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/mapa.html): Visual
  subway-style roadmap. A common economics trunk (origins of money, fiat
  history, Bitcoin standard, double-spend problem) splits into two parallel
  lines with placeholder chapters for the non-technical and technical tracks,
  plus side-branch deep-dives (SHA-256, ECDSA).
- [Origens do dinheiro (artigo de exemplo)](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/artigo.html):
  First chapter on the common trunk. Why money exists, the double-coincidence
  of wants, Carl Menger's spontaneous-institution view, properties of good
  money (durability, divisibility, portability, scarcity, verifiability), and
  the lead-in to Bitcoin's core question.
- [Sobre o projeto](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/sobre.html): Author bio,
  motivation (libertarian community talks about Bitcoin without explaining
  it), how to contribute.

### English

- [Home / Landing](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/en/): English overview.
- [Content map](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/en/map.html): English roadmap.
- [Origins of money (sample chapter)](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/en/article.html):
  English version of the first chapter on the common trunk.
- [About the project](https://comofuncionabitcoin.com/en/about.html): English
  author bio and project rationale.

## Key topics covered (and planned)

- The origins and function of money (Mengerian view)
- The history of fiat and government money debasement (Rothbard)
- The Bitcoin standard and digital scarcity (Ammous)
- The double-spending problem and why digital money was previously impossible
- Hash functions and Merkle trees (technical track)
- Digital signatures and ECDSA (technical track)
- Proof of Work and decentralized consensus (technical track)
- Mempool, UTXOs, and wallets (technical track)
- Side deep-dives: SHA-256 internals, ECDSA / secp256k1 internals
